C-u C-/Undoundo with a universal argument is selective undo: it walks the document history back until the region's text differs, winds the history forward again so nothing outside the region moves, and puts just the region back to the older text — the effect of undoing the most recent change inside the regionportedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Undo.html#index-C_002du-C_002d_002f
C-u C-SPCMark RingC-u C-SPC pops the mark ring: set_mark_command asks cx.prefix_arg() and runs pop_to_mark when an argument is present, instead of setting a markportedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Mark-Ring.html#index-C_002du-C_002dSPC
C-u C-c C-w (Fortran mode)Fortran ColumnsC-c C-w reads the universal argument: without one it is fortran-window-create-momentarily (the column-72 marker is taken down by the next key), with one it is fortran-window-create — the marker stays up and you carry on editing with itportedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Fortran-Columns.html#index-C_002du-C_002dc-C_002dw-_0028Fortran-mode_0029
C-u C-x C-xDisabled Transient MarkC-u C-x C-x exchanges point and mark WITHOUT reactivating the region: flip_selections asks cx.prefix_arg() and leaves Select mode when one is presentportedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Disabled-Transient-Mark.html#index-C_002du-C_002dx-C_002dx
C-u C-x v =Old Revisionsgit_diff now reads cx.prefix_arg() — Emacs's (interactive "P") — exactly as vc.el's `historic` argument works: with a prefix argument it prompts `vc-diff — older revision:` then `Newer revision (default: current source):` and shows `git diff OLD [NEW] -- <file>` for the current file; without one it opens the side-by-side buffer-vs-HEAD viewer. The prefix argument comes from `C-u` in the emacs preset (universal_argument) or `SPC u` in the spacemacs default.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Old-Revisions.html#index-C_002du-C_002dx-v-_003d
C-u C-x v DOld RevisionsThe tree-wide half of the same mechanism: vc_root_diff with a prefix argument hands over to vc-root-version-diff, prompting for the two revisions and running `git diff OLD [NEW]` over the whole tree; without one it diffs the working tree against HEAD.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Old-Revisions.html#index-C_002du-C_002dx-v-D
C-u M-;Comment CommandsC-u M-; kills the comment on the line (comment-dwim with an argument): toggle_comments asks cx.prefix_arg() and runs comment_kill when one is presentportedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Comment-Commands.html#index-C_002du-M_002d_003b
C-u TABMulti-line Indentemacs C-u TAB (indent-for-tab-command with a numeric argument). indent_sexp_rigidly (commands.rs) already reindented the current line with the tree-sitter indent and shifted every other line of the parenthetical grouping starting on it by that same delta, leaving lines that start inside a string alone; it was registered but unreachable from a key. smart_tab now tests cx.prefix_arg() before indent-line-function and dispatches to it, so TAB under a prefix argument is the grouping shifter whatever function plain TAB would run — matching the Multi-line Indent manual node: 'TAB with a numeric argument reindents the current line as usual, then reindents by the same amount all the lines in the parenthetical grouping starting on the current line.' TAB reaches smart_tab through the emacs preset's tab -> emmet_expand, which falls back to it.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Multi_002dline-Indent.html#index-C_002du-TAB

SPC (GDB Breakpoints buffer)Breakpoints Buffer`SPC` in the GDB Breakpoints buffer is gdb-toggle-breakpoint's enable/disable: the breakpoint is withdrawn from the adapter (removed from Editor::breakpoints and setBreakpoints re-sent) but stays listed with `n` in the Enb column, and a second SPC re-arms it with its condition intact — gdb's `disable`/`enable`, not `delete`.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Breakpoints-Buffer.html#index-SPC-_0028GDB-Breakpoints-buffer_0029

SPC (completion)Completion CommandsSPC in a completing read runs Prompt::complete_word — it completes to the longest common prefix but stops at the first word separator past what is typed, so a second SPC completes the next word. mouse-1Mouse Commandsmouse-set-point: mouse-1 on text moves point to the click. ui/editor.rs's Down(Left) arm runs this command, so the command really is the handlerportedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Mouse-Commands.html#index-mouse_002d1
mouse-1 (mode line)Mode Line Mousemouse-1 on a mode line selects the window it belongs to (mouse_select_window acts on Editor::last_mouse_view, the window the click named). On the mode line of a window that has one below it the press also starts a drag that moves the boundary, changing the heights above and below; the resize clamps at the minimum pane size and never deletes a window.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Mode-Line-Mouse.html#index-mouse_002d1-_0028mode-line_0029
mouse-1 (scroll bar)Mode Line Mousepressing mouse-1 on the vertical scroll bar moves the window to that point in the buffer and keeps following the pointer until the button is released, even once it leaves the bar. The handler records the click as a fraction of the bar and dispatches through scroll-bar-drag, so the command really is the scroll bar's handler; point is pulled to the new top line when the scroll leaves it above the windowportedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Mode-Line-Mouse.html#index-mouse_002d1-_0028scroll-bar_0029
mouse-1 in the minibuffer (Incremental Search)Repeat IsearchClicking mouse-1 on the search prompt moves the prompt cursor to the clicked column and switches the running search into edit mode — RET resumes searching with the edited string (Prompt::isearch_edit_string in ui/prompt.rs). The static command of the same name is the M-e / M-x form of the same behaviour.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Repeat-Isearch.html#index-mouse_002d1-in-the-minibuffer-_0028Incremental-Search_0029
mouse-2Mouse Commandsmouse-yank-at-click: mouse-2 moves point to the click and inserts the kill ring's top there (ui/editor.rs's Down(Middle) arm runs it)portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Mouse-Commands.html#index-mouse_002d2
mouse-2 (GDB Breakpoints buffer)Breakpoints BufferThe middle mouse button on a row of the GDB Breakpoints buffer does the same as RET (gdb-goto-breakpoint): the clicked row becomes current and its source line is visited. Handled in the component's Event::Mouse arm on MouseEventKind::Down(MouseButton::Middle).portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Breakpoints-Buffer.html#index-mouse_002d2-_0028GDB-Breakpoints-buffer_0029
mouse-2 (mode line)Mode Line Mousemouse-2 on a mode line expands that window to fill the frame (delete-other-windows). The press and release must land on the same mode line, and it runs ahead of the middle-click paste.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Mode-Line-Mouse.html#index-mouse_002d2-_0028mode-line_0029
mouse-2 in the minibuffer (Incremental search)Isearch YankMiddle-clicking the search prompt while a search is running appends the selection (the '+' register, the same text C-y takes) to the search string and re-runs the search; an empty clipboard reports so. Handled in the prompt's isearch (ui/prompt.rs); the static command of the same name is the M-x form.portedhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Isearch-Yank.html#index-mouse_002d2-in-the-minibuffer-_0028Incremental-search_0029

C-h 4 iMisc HelpC-h 4 i is emacs `info-other-window` (info.el:780-787), whose interactive spec prompts for a file name only under a non-numeric prefix arg; with no prefix it opens the Info directory Top node in another window, reusing an existing window (display-buffer with `inhibit-same-window`, info.el:826-830) and splitting only when the frame has one window — all three confirmed by driving `emacs -Q -nw` in a pty. zmax's `info_search_other_window` (commands.rs:38822) is now written to match: it renders `(dir)Top` via `render_info_node` (commands.rs:15109, shells `info -o - "(dir)Top"`), then `display_other_window` (commands.rs:15125) focuses an existing non-focused view — splitting only when this is the sole window — and `show_text_in_scratch` replaces that view's buffer; a render failure sets an error and leaves the layout alone, and there is no picker to abort. NOT YET VERIFIED BEHAVIORALLY: the working tree does not compile (unrelated `shell_impl_async` and `ui/merge.rs` errors), and the last built binary predates this change and still shows the old `info --apropos` picker seeded at point, so the three divergences are closed in source only. Remaining divergences regardless: the target is a plain scratch buffer, not an Info-mode `*info*` buffer (no n/p/u/l navigation, no Info history, and each invocation re-renders rather than re-displaying an existing buffer as info.el:821-824 does); the prefix-argument forms (`read-file-name "Info file name: "` and the numeric `*info*<N>` buffer) are unimplemented; and the key is bound only in the spacemacs preset (spacemacs.rs:314) — the emacs preset binds C-h to delete_char_backward (emacs.rs:130) and has no help prefix, so C-h 4 i is unreachable there.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Misc-Help.html#index-C_002dh-4-i

C-wheel-downText Scalezmax scales the whole terminal, not the buffer. `text_scale_decrease` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:38947) mutates one global `editor.text_scale` counter and calls `emit_font_step(-1)` (commands.rs:38924-38934) which writes xterm `OSC 50 ;#-1` — a terminal-wide font-menu step, so every window/pane changes together and emacs's buffer-local `text-scale-mode` face-height (two windows at different scales) is unreachable. Terminals with no font menu ignore the sequence, so the command can be a pure no-op while still printing `text scale: -1`. Two further gaps the first skeptic missed: (a) the counter is unbounded while the terminal's font menu clamps at its smallest entry, so `editor.text_scale` desyncs from the real font and `text_scale_apply`/`text_scale_set` (commands.rs:61451-61466), which compute deltas from that counter, then step the wrong amount; (b) the C-wheel branch is only reached…partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Text-Scale.html#index-C_002dwheel_002ddown
C-wheel-upText ScaleThree gaps. (a) Effect is not per-buffer text scaling at all: text_scale_increase (commands.rs:38939) bumps one global editor.text_scale counter and emits terminal-wide OSC 50 #+1 (emit_font_step, commands.rs:38926); nothing reads editor.text_scale except the text_scale_set/adjust/mode bookkeeping (commands.rs:61445-61510), no renderer consults it, and emit_font_step's own doc says terminals without a font menu ignore the sequence — so on most terminals C-wheel-up produces only the status line "text scale: +1". The counter is also shared in effect with frame_zoom_in/out (commands.rs:38966+), which drive the same OSC steps, so the two families interfere and text_scale_reset resets globally rather than per window. emacs mouse-wheel-text-scale scales only the buffer in the window under the pointer. (b) Unadmitted runtime shadow: bufferline_y is initialized to 0 (ui/editor.rs:446) and only…partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Text-Scale.html#index-C_002dwheel_002dup

C-x 4 fVisitingEmacs `C-x 4 f` / `C-x 4 C-f` (find-file-other-window). The `C-x 4` submap now exists in the emacs preset (keymap/emacs.rs:210-219) as well as spacemacs (keymap/spacemacs.rs:97-110), with f, C-f, b, 0 and `.`; those five bindings match GNU Emacs 30.2 (`key-binding` confirms each). `find_file_other_window` (commands.rs:55339) was rewritten to look for a view other than the focused one and, when one exists, focus it and build the picker with `Action::Replace` plus a `with_on_abort` that restores the previous focus, falling back to `Action::HorizontalSplit` only when this is the sole window — matching the docstring's "creates a new window or reuses an existing one". UNVERIFIED AND NOT RUNNABLE: none of this has ever been executed. The built binary predates the edits (C-x 4 is unbound there; the old code still goes 2 windows -> 3, reproduced under pty), and the working tree does not compile, so the reuse path has not been driven even once. KNOWN DIVERGENCES THAT REMAIN: - >=3 windows: emacs reuses the next window in cyclic order (verified: with focus on the middle of 3, emacs reused the window below and left the first alone). `views().find(|id| *id != focus)` picks the first view in arena order (tree.rs:608), so with focus off the arena-first view zmax replaces a different window's buffer than emacs. The two rules agree only at exactly 2 windows. - Focus is moved when the picker OPENS; emacs reads the filename in its interactive spec with the original window still selected and switches only on RET. The abort end-state is restored, but the mid-prompt state differs. - The workspace picker enumerates existing files, so it cannot visit a not-yet-existing path; emacs's prompt passes `confirm-nonexistent-file-or-buffer` and can.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Visiting.html#index-C_002dx-4-f

Driven end-to-end in a pty under `keymap = "emacs"` against GNU Emacs 30.2 as oracle, it matches abbrev.el's `inverse-add-abbrev` (lines 427-444) on four points: it prompts `Expansion for Mode abbrev "<name>": ` per abbrev.el:436; it stores the key downcased per `(define-abbrev table (downcase name) exp)` at :441 (verified observably — defining from `FOO` then expanding a typed lowercase `foo` hits); it runs the trailing `(save-excursion (goto-char end) (expand-abbrev))` at :442-444, replacing the word in-buffer with the expansion; and it honours `(interactive "p")` including negative counts, with C-u 2 / C-u 3 / C-u -1 selecting the same word as the oracle ("EXPANDED two", "XX bb cc", "aa ZZ cc"). Known divergence: the expansion is inserted verbatim. abbrev_do_expand (commands.rs:20739) applies the replacement as a plain Transaction with no case adjustment, so abbrev.el:865-884 — upcase-initials-region/upcase-region when the abbrev name is all-caps, capitalize-first-initial when it merely contains caps — is unported. `hello FOO` yields "hello fungible object" where emacs yields "hello Fungible Object"; `hello Foo` yields "hello fungible object" where emacs yields "hello Fungible object". Only all-lowercase abbrev names round-trip identically. Unrelated but adjacent: C-e in the emacs preset leaves the cursor on the final character rather than past it (col 1:9 on a 9-char line), so a C-e-then-C-x-a-i-l sequence defines the wrong span ("fo" instead of "foo"). That belongs to the move-end-of-line binding, not to this command — with the cursor at true point-max this command is exact.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Defining-Abbrevs.html#index-C_002dx-a-i-l
C-x a lDefining Abbrevs`C-x a l` is bound to `add_mode_abbrev` in the emacs preset's INSERT keymap (`C-x a i l` -> inverse), and the command ports abbrev.el's `add-abbrev` prompts and word-extraction faithfully: at an equal point position it reproduces emacs 30.2 byte-for-byte, including trailing whitespace — no-arg takes one word back, ARG>0 takes ARG words back, negative ARG prompts `Undefine Mode abbrev: `, an existing definition prompts `NAME expands into "EXP"; redefine? `, and the name is stored downcased. The region clause (ARG 0 / active region) is implemented and works when the region comes from `C-x h`. It is NOT reachable the way emacs users reach it: `C-SPC` enters Select mode, whose keymap (keymap/emacs.rs:261-281) binds no `C-x` prefix, so `C-x a l` is inert with a region active. With no user region, ARG 0 silently defines a one-character abbrev from the helix block cursor instead of erroring `The mark is not set now`. `only-global-abbrevs` does not exist, so the redirect to the global table is unimplemented; mode tables are in-memory only (no `abbrev_file_name` persistence) and are keyed by document language / `fundamental` rather than an emacs major-mode name. Unrelated to this command but affecting its documented workflow: `C-e` (`goto_line_end`) stops one character short of emacs `end-of-line`, so `C-e` then `C-x a l` captures a truncated expansion.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Defining-Abbrevs.html#index-C_002dx-a-l

C-x w dDisplaying Buffers`C-x w d` (toggle-window-dedication) is implemented in the SPACEMACS keymap only (keymap/spacemacs.rs:555); it is unbound in the emacs preset, where the keys self-insert into the buffer and, because zmax autosaves, write to the file. Dedication is a real tri-state on the view (`View::dedicated_strong`), and the echo string reproduces emacs's own "Window is {no longer|now|now strongly} dedicated to buffer %s" verbatim -- the plain toggle is byte-identical to emacs 30.2. Verified matching: a strongly dedicated window refuses a buffer switch (zmax echoes "Window is strongly dedicated to its buffer"; emacs signals "Window is dedicated to '<buf>'" -- same refusal, different wording), and a weakly dedicated window causes `display-buffer`-style redirection into an existing other window instead of splitting a third, falling back to a split only when no other window exists. NOT matching: the prefix-argument mapping is inverted relative to emacs. emacs gives STRONG dedication only for a raw cons prefix (bare `C-u`) and leaves a NUMERIC prefix weak (`C-u 4` sets dedicated-p=4 and prints "now dedicated"); zmax treats any leading count (2, 4, 16) as strong and a bare `C-u` as plain/weak. Emacs's default `toggle-window-dedicated-flag` value `interactive` -- a third state that auto-clears on a manual buffer switch -- is not modelled.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Displaying-Buffers.html#index-C_002dx-w-d

I (Dired)Operating on Files`I` (`dired-do-info`) is bound and reachable. Dired's `handle_event` strips `KeyModifiers::SHIFT` from any `KeyCode::Char` before dispatch, so the uppercase bindings written as bare `key!('I')` fire from a real key press (verified: `I` runs the handler, `C` prompts `Copy to:`, `S` prompts `Symlink to:`). The handler shells `info --file <path> --output -` and shows the captured stdout -- the Top node only -- via `show_text_in_scratch`, then sets `close_requested`, which now pops the Dired overlay from the non-prompt key path so the scratch buffer is left visible and focused rather than hidden behind Dired. What still differs from Emacs: the result is an ordinary scratch buffer in `plain text`, not `(Info Narrow)`. Emacs's `(info FILE)` builds `*info* (a2ps) Top` with a live navigation graph; here `n`/`p`/`u`/`l`, `Info-menu` and follow-reference do nothing (`n` and `u` leave the cursor at 1:1). Rendering is info(1)'s raw output, so the node header line `File: ..., Node: Top, Next: ...` appears as buffer text where Emacs lifts it into a header-line, and menu entries keep their literal `::` where Emacs hides it and makes the entry a link. Closing this needs a per-buffer major-mode keymap mechanism zmax does not have, since binding `n`/`p`/`u`/`l` in a normal document would collide with editing keys. Separately, the missing-node case is currently invisible: when `info` exits 0 with empty output the code sets the error `info <name>: no such node or anchor: Top`, and Dired correctly stays open, but Dired's own footer occupies the status line so the message is never rendered. Emacs shows `No such node or anchor: Top` in the echo area at once (and without the `info <name>: ` prefix).partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Operating-on-Files.html#index-I-_0028Dired_0029

M-s f C-s (Dired)Dired Navigation`M-s f C-s` (dired-isearch-filenames) is a port of Emacs's isearch state machine over a character-addressed position space: point is `(row, byte offset into that row's file name)`, and `isearch-cmds`, `isearch-opoint`, `isearch-barrier`, direction and wrap flags are all carried (zmax-term/src/ui/dired.rs:281-314, 1198-1442, router 2767-2830). Verified key-for-key against GNU Emacs 30.2 driving `dired-isearch-filenames` on the same 7-name fixture: every repeated match inside one file name is its own `C-s` stop (a 13-press `a` walk produces the identical row sequence, 3 stops in `aaa.txt`); typing after a repeat re-searches from the near end of the current match, so it fails in place with "Failing" instead of dragging point back to an earlier row; the first `C-r` only reverses direction and re-finds the same match from the other side (`isearch-repeat-on-direction-change` nil); a repeat past the last match fails once and wraps on the next press (`isearch-wrap-pause` t), and the prompt reproduces Emacs's "Failing"/"Wrapped"/"Overwrapped"/"case-sensitive" annotations and the " backward" suffix. `DEL` pops the command stack, `C-g` quits a successful search to the origin and rubs a failing one back to the last success, case folding follows `isearch-no-upper-case-p`, and `C-s` on an empty pattern takes the previous string off the search ring. Still partial on one point: the intra-name offset exists only while a search is live -- Dired's own point is a row, and `begin_input` opens every search at column 0 of the selected row (dired.rs:1121), while Emacs opens at point. So a search that exits with RET in the middle of a name does not hand its position to the next search: emacs `a C-s C-s RET` then a new search and `a` lands on the second entry, zmax re-matches inside the first one. There is no match-count echo, which is correct -- `isearch-lazy-count` is nil by default.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Dired-Navigation.html#index-M_002ds-f-C_002ds-_0028Dired_0029
M-s f M-C-s (Dired)Dired Navigation`M-s f C-M-s` (dired-isearch-filenames-regexp) opens an incremental filename search whose pattern is compiled as an Emacs regexp: `emacs_regexp_to_rust` (zmax-term/src/ui/dired.rs:324) escapes bare `(`, `)`, `|`, `{`, `}` to literals and turns `\(`, `\)`, `\|`, `\{`, `\}` into the operators, maps `\<`/`\>`/`\_<`/`\_>` to `\b`, `` \` ``/`\'` to `\A`/`\z`, drops `\=`, treats a backslash inside `[...]` as a literal member, and returns None for a trailing backslash; an uncompilable pattern leaves the state untouched so point holds (dired.rs:1238-1240). `isearch_no_upper_case` (dired.rs:387) implements `isearch-no-upper-case-p` including the `[:upper:]`/`[:lower:]` check and the odd-backslash rule, and feeds `RegexBuilder::case_insensitive` (dired.rs:1182), so smart case applies. Verified against GNU Emacs 30.2 driven in a pty on a six-file fixture: `gamma|beta` and `ap(p)` are literal and fail with the "Failing" prompt while point holds, `gamma\|beta` alternates, `p{2}` is literal where `p\{2\}` repeats, `2$` anchors, `be[` holds point, lowercase `be` folds to reach `abe.txt` while `Be` stays case-sensitive and reaches `zBeta2`, and `C-s` on an empty pattern pulls the previous string off the regexp ring and moves point to it. Still partial: the incremental re-search anchor differs. Emacs re-searches from the search origin on every keystroke, so `beta\|` matches the empty alternative and snaps point to the top of the buffer, leaving `beta\|gamma` on `gamma.txt`; zmax continues forward from the current match and never moves point back, leaving it on `zbeta.txt` -- same keys, same fixture, valid regexp, different file. zmax also omits Emacs's echo-area sub-states "[incomplete input]", "[Trailing backslash]" and the "Pending" prefix (the "Failing" prefix is present and agrees), anchors `` \` ``/`\'` to the file name rather than to the whole dired buffer, and does not translate syntax classes `\sX`/`\SX`, category classes `\cX`/`\CX` or backreferences `\1`-`\9`, which fail to compile and therefore hold point. Unrelated to this spec but affecting which row a search lands on, zmax sorts the listing case-insensitively where Emacs uses byte order.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Dired-Navigation.html#index-M_002ds-f-M_002dC_002ds-_0028Dired_0029

Complete Current StatementIntelliJ IDEA default keymap: Cmd Shift EnterComplete Current Statement (Cmd-Shift-Enter) = complete_current_statement, bound under the Emacs major-mode prefix C-c as `C-c ;` — active in Insert, Normal AND Select (spacemacs), so it fires while typing like JetBrains. For a `fn`/`if`/`for`/`while`/`match`/`impl`/... header (line_opens_block) in a brace language (lang_uses_braces), closes any open `(`/`[` then inserts `{ body }` and drops the caret on the indented body line — e.g. `fn tommy()` -> `fn tommy() {<caret>}`, `while (1)` -> `while (1) {<caret>}`. Otherwise closes open brackets/parens, appends the terminator (`;` for semicolon languages via lang_uses_semicolons), and opens an indented line below. Brace vs semicolon are independent axes so brace-but-not-semicolon languages (Go, stryke) still get braces; an unknown/scratch buffer defaults to brace-capable (C-family). Core decision is the pure, unit-tested plan_complete_statement. Line-local heuristic (not full PSI).portedhttps://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/reference-keymap-mac-default.html

CTRL-Bcursor to begin of command-linec_CTRL-B — under the vim/spacemacs presets (`Editor::vim_semantics`, set at zmax-term/src/application.rs:253/:935) C-b moves the cursor to the beginning of the command line, the same as `<Home>`/C-a (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:1879, `move_start`). Verified against nvim: `:/b/Z/<C-B>s<CR>` on "abc" yields "aZc" in both. Applies to the `/` search prompt as well, since both share `Prompt::handle_event`. Under the helix/emacs presets C-b remains `backward-char` (prompt.rs:1880); `<Home>`, C-a and `<Left>` are unchanged.portedindex.txt:c_CTRL-B
CTRL-Csame as <Esc>CTRL-Cportedindex.txt:c_CTRL-C
CTRL-Dlist completions that match the pattern inc_CTRL-D lists the names matching the pattern in front of the cursor, per cmdline.txt: list_completion_before_cursor (prompt.rs:459) feeds completion_fn the slice &self.line[..self.cursor] instead of the whole line, clears the selection, resets wild_press, and leaves the line untouched. Verified in a pty against nvim 0.12.4: ':setx' with the cursor on the 'x' lists set/setglobal/setlocal (nvim: set/setfiletype/setglobal/setlocal) and leaves the line as ':setx'; before the change the whole-line pattern 'setx' matched nothing and listed nothing. The cursor-at-end control (':set' + C-D) is unchanged and produces the identical list. Enter after C-D executes the typed line, so nothing is selected, and the cmdline_eval short-circuit is kept, so the nested '=' prompt of c_CTRL-\_e still lists nothing. What still differs is not in this arm: the candidate set itself comes from zmax's fuzzy matcher over a merged vim+emacs command namespace, so the list is far longer than nvim's prefix-matched ex commands and omits setfiletype (an alias of :language); Tab/wildchar emits a byte-identical list, which places that divergence in the shared completion_fn. Long lists are also not paged the way nvim's '-- More --' prompt pages them. The Emacs-preset C-D delete-char arm (prompt.rs:1972) is unchanged and remains undriveable, since ':' does not open a prompt under :keymap emacs.portedindex.txt:c_CTRL-D
CTRL-Ecursor to end of command-lineCTRL-Eportedindex.txt:c_CTRL-E
CTRL-Gnext match when 'incsearch' is activec_CTRL-G: next match while 'incsearch' is live (ui/prompt.rs incsearch_cycle). vim presets only - in the Emacs presets C-g stays isearch-abortportedindex.txt:c_CTRL-G

CTRL-\ e {expr} replace the command line with the result of{expr}CTRL-\ e {expr} evaluates {expr} as an EXPRESSION (not a script) and replaces the whole command line with the result, driven and diffed against nvim 0.12.4 in a pty. Verified matching: string literals in either quote style, numbers, floats and dicts; getcmdline()/getcmdtype()/getcmdpos() readable from inside the expression, including type `/` at the search prompt (which zmax words "search:"); the doc's own `getcmdline() .. " Some()"` example; the cursor rule — unchanged mid-line, kept when the result is shorter (clamped to a char boundary), moved to the new end only when it was already at the end, and overridden by setcmdpos(); and the restore path on a failing expression, a syntax error, a reported-but-not-failing error such as `no_such_fn()` (E117), and <Esc>. The resulting line is a real command line: an expression yielding "set nonumber" executes on <CR>. Still differs from nvim: (1) a nested CTRL-\ e inside the expression prompt is honored instead of being inserted literally — vim types `^\e` into the expression and later executes the original line, zmax clears the expression line and ultimately executes nothing; (2) a List result renders as `[1, 2]` instead of vim's NUL-joined `1^@2^@`.partialindex.txt:c_CTRL-\_e
{char1} <BS> {char2}enter digraph when 'digraph' is ondigraph entry via C-k (insert_digraph); different input model than {char1}<BS>{char2}partialindex.txt:c_digraph

.repeat last change with count replaced withrepeat the last change. Broader than the old note claimed: verified against neovim, 19 of 20 cases match - x, dd, 2dd, dw, 3dw, de, dt<c>, diw, ciw, A, o, r, ~, J, >>, yy/p/P, counts, and '..'. The one gap is a *counted* charwise delete whose count runs past the line: `3x` on a 2-char line clamps correctly on its own (3x/9x match), but dot-repeating it deletes the newline and merges the lines (`3xj0.` -> nvim '||L3|L4', zmax '|L3|L4'), so the replay is not line-bounded the way the original was.partialindex.txt:.

CTRL-Lredraw screenvim CTRL-L = clear and redraw the screen; the default keymap deliberately keeps emacs's recenter on C-l (pinned by keymap::vim::tests::emacs_readline_keys_bound). The redraw itself is :redraw.partialindex.txt:CTRL-L
CTRL-Xsubtract N from number at/after cursorvim `CTRL-X` decrements the number at or after the cursor. Not reachable in the shipped keymap: keymap.rs:14 ships spacemacs, where `C-x` is the emacs prefix (spacemacs.rs:65) and opens a submap — the key waits for a second keystroke instead. Measured against nvim: `3<C-x>` on 'num 7 here' gives 'num 4' there and leaves 'num 7' here, the count and the C-x being swallowed by the pending submap. The capability is present as `g C-x` (vim.rs:894), which the keymap comment calls out deliberately. `C-a` is unshadowed and fully correct, counts, hex and negatives included — the pair is asymmetric. Same category as f/F/t/T being labelled jumps and s/S being sneak: a deliberate default, recorded not argued with.partialindex.txt:CTRL-X
F{char}cursor to the Nth occurrence of {char} tozmax binds the plain motion to a *labelled* jump (find_char_forward_label / jump_to_char_label), not vim's direct move: `fa` paints a label on every `a` and waits for a label key, where vim moves to the next `a` outright. Verified by driving the binary - after `fa` the cursor is still at 1:1 and the buffer is overlaid with labels; the following key is consumed as a label pick. The operator forms are vim-faithful (df/dF/dt/dT go through find_char_then and match vim byte-for-byte), so this is the plain motion only. Capability present, different model.partialindex.txt:F

["x]Sdelete N lines [into register x] and startvim S = cc (delete the line, keep its indent, start insert). The substitute itself is correct - verified against neovim with `:set vim-sneak false`: SQ gives ' Q' and 2SQ collapses two lines to ' Q', both matching nvim, as does ccQ. Partial only because it is not reachable by default: `s`/`S` are bound to sneak_or_substitute_line and the shipped default has vim-sneak on (editor.rs:1484, documented at :459 as overriding s/S with a two-character jump), so bare S starts a sneak.partialindex.txt:S
["x]c{motion}delete Nmove text [into register x] and`{d,c,y}{/,?}pat<CR>` runs a search as an operator motion. Verified against nvim 0.12.4 by driving both editors. Working: the base exclusive motion (`0d/charlie` -> "charlie delta echo", per pattern.txt:19 "|exclusive|"); backward `d?pat`; `[count]` (`02d/X`); the character search-offsets `e` (inclusive of the match end, `0d/charlie/e` -> " delta echo"), `s`, and `b[N]`, in both `d` and `c` forms; the no-match abort (`d/NOPE`, `c/NOPE`, `y/NOPE` all leave the buffer intact and set "Pattern not found", confirmed with an `A!!` marker as positive control since zmax autosaves); and `["x]` register routing — `"ay/pat` / `"ad/pat` now deposit the span in the named register instead of clobbering it with the pattern, because the prompt's history register is pinned to '/'. NOT working: the bare `[±]N` LINEWISE offset is off by exactly one line, in both directions. `0d/gamma/+1` on a 4-line buffer should empty the file but leaves "delta"; `0d/gamma/-1` should leave "gamma\ndelta" but leaves "beta\ngamma\ndelta"; `/+0`, `/1` and `/beta/+2` fail the same way. apply_search_offset lands the cursor on the first grapheme of the offset line, so the span ends at that boundary and extend_to_line_bounds snaps without including the target line. Separately, `c0` and `y0` gained the `extend_backward_exclusive_vim` step that `d0` already had, so all three now stop before the cursor's character: on "alpha bravo charlie" with the cursor at column 6, `c0` yields "XXbravo charlie", `y0` yanks exactly "alpha ", `d0` yields "bravo charlie". The `y0` change was not part of the original gap list but is confirmed correct against nvim. Caveat: verified on a HEAD + this-change-only build. The repo working tree does not currently compile (unrelated concurrent edits) and target/debug/zmax predates this change, so this needs a rebuild and re-drive in-tree.partialindex.txt:c
["x]d{motion}delete Nmove text [into register x]vim {motion} takes ANY motion; zmax has no operator-pending mode and enumerates the motions in each operator's submap. Standard motions, text objects (i/a) and marks (`/') work. Verified missing or wrong against vim 9.2 by driving both: d/pat (search) and dn do nothing; d% (matching paren) does nothing; d0 deletes one char too many ('harlie' vs vim's 'charlie'). c{motion}/y{motion} share the submap shape.partialindex.txt:d

Partial only because it is not reachable by default: `s` is sneak_or_substitute_char and the shipped default has vim-sneak on, so bare s starts a two-character jump. Same deliberate-override category as f/F/t/T being labelled jumps.partialindex.txt:s

f{char}cursor to Nth occurrence of {char} to thef/F/t/T are now confined to the cursor's line in the vim preset, per motion.txt "2. Left-right motions" ("These commands move the cursor to the specified column in the current line"). `find_nth_char_on_line` clips the rope scan to [line_start, line_end_char_index) and returns None when the search start is already off that line; `find_char`/`find_char_then` select it via a `line_bounded` flag, the four `vim_find_*`/`vim_till_*` commands are bound in keymap/vim.rs, and `;`/`,` inherit the bound through `apply_find_char`. Verified against nvim 0.12.4: gg0fa on "xbxbxb\nyayaya" stays at 1:1 (pre-fix binary jumped to 2:2), backward `Fb`/`Tb` on a line with no match do not move, and `;` will not repeat onto another line. Count, inclusive landing, count-overflow no-move and f-based `;`/`,` all match (fa, 2fa, 3fa, 9fa, fa;, fa,), as does non-adjacent `t` ("xyzaqa": ta->1:3, 2ta->1:5). helix's own find_next_char keeps the whole-buffer scan for the default preset and emacs zap-to-char stays unbounded. Two divergences remain. (a) `t` still skips a target that is already adjacent: on "yayaya" from column 0 nvim's `ta` does not move, zmax lands at 1:3. This is not a 'cpo-;' question — cpo-; governs only `;`/`,` repeat of a t search, and nvim's default 'cpo' omits ';', which is why nvim's `ta;` does skip while plain `ta` does not; zmax skips in both. It also breaks 2ta, ta;, ta, and dta (nvim deletes 1 char, zmax 3). (b) A find that matches nothing on the line, or whose count overflows, leaves the width-1 selection intact instead of aborting the operator, so `dfz`, `d9fa` and `gg0 dfa` each delete the character under the cursor where nvim leaves the buffer untouched; zmax autosaves the result. (b) predates this change (the pre-fix binary does the same for dfz) but the new line bound now routes cross-line misses into it. book/src/generated/static-cmd.md is stale for the four new commands.partialindex.txt:f
g@{motion}call 'operatorfunc'g@: call 'operatorfunc'. vim applies it to the region the following motion covers; zmax applies it to the current selection (the engine already has that region), so the {motion} argument is not readpartialindex.txt:g@
gmgo to character at middle of the screenlinevim `gm` is `g0` plus half a screenwidth (`:h gm`), clamping to the line's end when the line is shorter — on 'alpha one' it lands on the last char. zmax binds it to goto_line_middle, which is the middle of the line's *text* (commands.rs:3229) — that is `gM`'s job, and `gM` is bound to the very same command (vim.rs:988 / :1018). Measured against nvim: `gmx` gives 'alpha on' there and 'alph one' here; `gMx` matches.partialindex.txt:gm
gq{motion}format Nmove textvim gq{motion} = reformat; zmax reformats the motion range via LSP formatter.partialindex.txt:gq

gw{motion}format Nmove text and keep cursorgw{motion} reflows to 'text-width' with the built-in wrapper and, per change.txt:1447, ignores 'formatprg'/'formatexpr' — both driven against nvim: with formatprg=rev and with formatexpr=setline(v:lnum,'XX'), zmax gw produces the same buffer as nvim gw while gq is filtered. The cursor is now restored to the same character in the reflowed text (the old 1:1 collapse is gone): 2G10|gwap, 1G1|/4G20|/3G39|gwap, gw}, gwj, gww, gwgw, gwip and gwG all reproduce nvim's cursor and buffer exactly. Still divergent when the cursor starts on a BLANK: the restore indexes the cursor among the region's non-blank characters, which cannot name a space, so it rounds forward — 1G6|gwap gives 1:7 where nvim gives 1:6 (same for 2G5|, 3G9|, 3G20|, 1G6|gw}), and 4G14|gwap lands 6:1 against nvim's 5:26. {Visual}gw is unchanged and still differs (2G10|Vjgw 4:19 vs nvim 3:20; backwards-linewise and charwise visual also reflow a different region).partialindex.txt:gw

zAopen a closed fold or close an open foldvim `zA` toggles the folds at the cursor recursively; zmax binds it to fold_toggle — literally the same command as `za` (vim.rs:1083 `"a" => fold_toggle` / :1094 `"A" => fold_toggle`), so the recursion the uppercase form exists for is absent.partialindex.txt:zA
zCclose folds recursivelyvim `zC` closes the folds at the cursor recursively; zmax binds it to fold_close, the same command as `zc`. vim.rs:1087 `"C" => fold_close, // zC close folds recursively (approx)`.partialindex.txt:zC
zDdelete folds recursivelyvim `zD` deletes the folds at the cursor recursively; zmax binds it to fold_delete, which deletes the one at the cursor. vim.rs:1092 `"D" => fold_delete, // zD delete folds recursively (approx: at cursor)`.partialindex.txt:zD
zGtemporarily mark word as correctly spelledzg/zw write the word (lowercased) to 'spellfile' — the first name only — and zug/zuw remove it by rewriting the file, where vim turns the entry into a comment line. zG/zW/zuG/zuW drive a session-only internal word list that is never persisted; this was verified by driving the binary (]s skips a zG'd word, stops on a zW'd word, and neither the spellfile nor ~/.zmax/spell-bad is touched), so the earlier "zG writes the spellfile" defect is gone. Two parts of the zg entry are still unimplemented: a count does not select the Nth 'spellfile' entry (2zg writes the first file, vim writes the second), and zg in Visual mode adds nothing, where vim adds the selected characters including white space. :spellgood!/:spellwrong!/:spellrare!/:spellundo! exist in source and are registered in TYPABLE_COMMAND_LIST, but are not in any built binary and have never been executed; driving :spellgood! against the shipped binary is a silent no-op. :spellrare and :spellrare! flag words as plain bad — zmax has no separate rare class, so vim's rare highlighting/BAD[rare] classification is not reproduced.partialindex.txt:zG
zNset 'foldenable'vim `zN` sets 'foldenable' (restoring folds to 'foldlevel'); zmax binds it to fold_close_all, the same command as `zM` (vim.rs:1090 / :1099), which closes everything regardless of foldlevel.partialindex.txt:zN
zOopen folds recursivelyvim `zO` opens the folds at the cursor recursively; zmax binds it to fold_open, the same command as `zo`, which opens the one fold at the cursor. The binding says so itself: vim.rs:1085 `"O" => fold_open, // zO open folds recursively (approx: open at cursor)`.partialindex.txt:zO
zWtemporarily mark word as incorrectly spelledvim `zW` marks a word bad for this session only; zmax binds it to spell_add_bad, which persists. vim.rs:1074 `"W" => spell_add_bad, // zW temporarily bad (approx)`.partialindex.txt:zW
zXre-apply 'foldlevel'vim `zX` re-applies 'foldlevel' and opens just enough folds to reveal the cursor; zmax binds it to fold_open_all, the same command as `zR` (vim.rs:1089 / :1100), which opens everything.partialindex.txt:zX
zitoggle 'foldenable'vim `zi` toggles the 'foldenable' option, opening or closing every fold in the buffer at once; zmax binds it to fold_toggle, the same command as `za`, which toggles the single fold at the cursor (vim.rs:1095). Different command, not a weaker one.partialindex.txt:zi
zswhen 'wrap' off scroll horizontally toNormal-mode `zs` matches nvim: driven at column 100 on a 300-char line with 'nowrap', zmax scrolls so the cursor sits at the left edge (leftcol 99), same as nvim v0.12.4; `zh`/`zH` also scroll left as vim does. In Visual/Select mode the shipped binary ignores the entire z view family (`zs`, `ze`, `zh`, `zl`, `zH`, `zL`, `zz`, `zt`, `zb`) — `v` then `zs` leaves the view exactly where `v` alone left it, whereas nvim sets leftcol=99 and keeps the highlighted area intact. A source edit adding those keys to the Visual `z` submap (keymap/vim.rs, next to the existing `zf`) is present in the working tree but uncommitted and unbuilt; the tree currently fails to compile for unrelated reasons, so the Visual-mode behaviour is unverified. Rightward horizontal scroll in Normal mode (`zl`/`zL` after `zs`) also appeared not to move the view, unlike nvim's `zL`; not confirmed. 'sidescroll' interaction not probed.partialindex.txt:zs
zuGundo |zG|Normal-mode zG/zW/zuG/zuW now implement nvim's two-list model correctly and this was confirmed by driving both editors. zG/zW (keymap/vim.rs:1169-1170) add to an in-memory internal word list (spell.rs:327/335) that is never persisted; zuG/zuW (vim.rs:1171-1172 -> spell_undo_internal -> spell::remove_internal, spell.rs:343) clear only that list. zug/zuw still route to spell_undo -> remove_user (spell.rs:351), which touches only the on-disk spell-good/spell-bad files. Driven against nvim 0.12.4 for all eight combinations (zg+zuG, zg+zug, zG alone, zG+zug, zG+zuG, zW+zuw, zW+zuW, zw+zuW), zmax matches the oracle on every one: a zg spellfile entry survives zuG, and a zG internal entry survives zug, exactly as spell.txt:98-104 specifies. What still differs: the ex-command forms `:spellgood!`, `:spellwrong!` and `:spellundo!` are silent no-ops. Their handlers (typed.rs:39037, :4149, :4230) do call the correct internal-list functions and are registered in the command table, but driving them over a pty produces no state change at all, while the non-bang `:spellgood`/`:spellwrong` work in the same session — so dispatch to the bang variants is broken upstream of the handler. Since nvim documents `:spellundo!` as "Like |zuW|" (spell.txt:144), the ex half of this exact distinction is still unimplemented in practice. Separately, the on-disk representation differs from vim by design: vim comments out an undone spellfile entry and flags bad words with `/!` in the same file, whereas zmax deletes the line and keeps bad words in a separate spell-bad file. Observable spell state is the same.partialindex.txt:zuG
zuWundo |zW|vim's `zuG`/`zuW` undo the *temporary* `zG`/`zW`; zmax binds them to spell_undo, the same command as `zug`/`zuw` (vim.rs:1076-1079). Moot in any case while `zG`/`zW` persist the word like `zg`/`zw` — see those specs.partialindex.txt:zuW
zxre-apply 'foldlevel' and do "zv"vim `zx` re-applies 'foldlevel' and then opens just enough folds to reveal the cursor; zmax binds it to fold_open. vim.rs:1067 `"x" => fold_open, // zx re-apply foldlevel and open enough to see cursor (approx)`.partialindex.txt:zx

C-x C-eLisp Eval [Emacs prefix, active in Spacemacs]`C-x C-e` runs `eval_last_sexp` (bound only in the spacemacs preset). It takes the sexp ending at `selection.primary().cursor(text)` — emacs's point, the left edge of the block cursor — so with the cursor on the second `(` of `(+ 1 2)(+ 10 20)` it evaluates the first form and echoes `3 (#o3, #x3, ?\C-c)`, as emacs does. An empty preceding range errors `elisp: end-of-file`, matching emacs's `(end-of-file)` signal. Integer results are echoed in emacs's `eval-expression-print-format` shape (simple.el:2003) — decimal, then `(#o…, #x…[, ?c])`, sign before magnitude for negatives, `prin1-char` forms `?\C-@` / `?\C-\[` / `?\C-_` / `?\C-?` for the controls and `?\(`-style escapes for `"'();[\]{}`, with the character part dropped past `eval-expression-print-maximum-character` (127). Verified byte-identical to `emacs -Q --batch --eval '(eval-expression-print-format N)'` on GNU Emacs 30.2 for 0, 3, 27, 32, 40, 65, 92, 127, 233 and -5. Non-integers echo the prin1 form alone; there is no `⇒ ` prefix. Prefix arguments follow `eval-expression-get-print-arguments` (simple.el:2087): any argument other than `nil` or a bare `-` inserts the printed text at point instead of echoing; `nil`/`0` keep the 127 character limit, `-`/`-1` lift it, any other argument suppresses the character form. Driven and matching for no-argument, `M-0` and `M-4`. The `-` and `-1` branches are code-correct but currently unreachable: the spacemacs preset routes no key to `negative-argument` (`M--` falls through as an unbound `<A-minus>`) and `universal-argument` is bound only in the emacs preset, which does not bind `C-x C-e`. `elisp--eval-defun-1`'s forced re-set (elisp-mode.el:1658) is only matched for `defvar`, and by accident of the evaluator rather than by design: `compile_defvar` (vendor/elisprs/src/compiler.rs:343) emits `SETVAR` unconditionally, so re-evaluating `(defvar v 2)` over `v = 99` yields 2 as in emacs. `defcustom` and `defface` are NOT special-cased and still diverge: re-evaluating a `defcustom` leaves the old value (emacs 2, zmax 99) and re-evaluating a `defface` leaves the old spec (emacs `((t :weight normal))`, zmax `((t :weight bold))`). Both forms do exist in the vendored evaluator — `vendor/elisprs/src/prelude.rs:5615` and `:5625`, a port of custom.el's declaration half — so closing this is a matter of porting `elisp--eval-defun-1`'s `custom-declare-variable` / `custom-declare-face` rewrites here, not vendor work. `NO-TRUNCATE` (the `print-length`/`print-level` lift a `0` argument implies) is also not implemented.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Lisp-Eval.html#index-C_002dx-C_002de

C-x \Select Input Method [Emacs prefix, active in Spacemacs]Three divergences, ordered by weight. (a) The chord is unbound in every shipped preset — zero `\` literals in keymap/spacemacs.rs, only A-\ and C-A-\ in keymap/emacs.rs — so C-x \ falls through the live C-x prefix and the command is name-only (A-x palette or `:activate-transient-input-method`). (b) Re-activation semantics, missed by the first skeptic and verified against upstream mule-cmds.el: emacs does `(setq previous-transient-input-method current-input-method)` unconditionally, so pressing C-x \ twice before typing makes the transient method its own predecessor and it survives the chunk permanently; zmax deliberately refuses that (`Some(state) if state.transient => state.previous`, commands.rs:59371-59374) and restores the pre-transient method instead. The comment declares the choice but it contradicts the source it claims to port. Related: emacs's exitfun removes only its own…partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Select-Input-Method.html#index-C_002dx-_005c
C-x a i lDefining Abbrevs [Emacs prefix, active in Spacemacs]Ports inverse-add-abbrev (lisp/abbrev.el:413-444) for C-x a i l. The name span comes from abbrev_nth_word_span, a faithful port of (forward-word (1+ (- arg))) / (skip-syntax-backward "^w") / (backward-word 1): verified against emacs 30.2 on "alpha beta gamma delta" for arg=1/2/0/-1 -> beta/alpha/gamma/delta, all matching (C-u and M-- reach it in the emacs preset; in spacemacs, evil shadows both, so use M-<digit>, matching real spacemacs). The prompt is verbatim emacs wording, 'Expansion for Mode abbrev "Foo": '. The definition is keyed on (downcase name), and lookup case-folds like abbrev--symbol (lowercase first, verbatim fallback), so defining on "Foo" and later typing "foo" + C-x ' expands. Redefining an existing name prompts 'Foo expands into "bar"; redefine? (y or n) ' with correct y/n semantics. After defining, the abbreviation standing in the buffer is expanded via abbrev_do_expand. Diverges from emacs in three ways. (a) The expansion is inserted verbatim; emacs case-adjusts it in abbrev-insert:861-882 whenever the buffer text differs in case from the stored (downcased) symbol -- which is this command's mainline path. Emacs turns "Foo " into "Bar baz " and "FOO " into "Bar Baz "; zmax produces "bar baz " for both. Only all-lowercase abbreviations round-trip identically. This lives in the shared expansion path, so plain C-x ' is affected too. (b) The redefine confirmation is a text-entry minibuffer requiring y+RET; emacs's y-or-n-p commits on the single "y" keystroke (y-or-n-p-insert-y inserts and exits). (c) Mode-local abbrev tables remain process-local (emacs_abbrev.rs:166), so a mode abbrev defined here is lost on restart while the global table persists.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Defining-Abbrevs.html#index-C_002dx-a-i-l
C-x a lDefining Abbrevs [Emacs prefix, active in Spacemacs]`C-x a l` (add-mode-abbrev) is implemented and driven end-to-end in the spacemacs preset: the expansion is the word before point or the active region, only the name is prompted for (`Mode abbrev that expands into "X": `, abbrev.el:367), the name is downcased before it is stored (abbrev.el:375), redefining an existing name asks `NAME expands into "OLD"; redefine? (y or n)` (abbrev.el:373), a negative prefix argument switches the prompt to `Undefine Mode abbrev: ` and removes the entry (abbrev.el:368), and a positive prefix argument takes N words back. Definitions land in a per-major-mode table keyed by zmax's language id (`.txt` -> `text`), separate from the file-backed global table, matching `only-global-abbrevs` = nil. Known divergences: `only-global-abbrevs` handling is newly written but unverified — the last runnable binary ignores the variable and still defines into the mode table when it is `t`, and the tree does not currently compile, so the reroute to the global table has never been observed; the emacs-style prefix argument (N words, 0 = region, negative = undefine) is only reachable in the emacs preset, since spacemacs normal state has no universal-argument and a bare count is ignored; in the emacs preset the `C-x a` submap is missing while the mark is active, so the region-as-expansion branch is unreachable there; and mode-local abbrev tables live only in memory for the session, where Emacs persists them through the abbrev file.partialhttps://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Defining-Abbrevs.html#index-C_002dx-a-l

S Psort by package name`S P` in the package menu sorts by package name; the key already worked and had no command to cite, so the sort now goes through PackageMenuView::sort_by, which both the key and package_menu_sort_by_name call. SPC m Ccheckout pull request (not for issues) (forge)forge-checkout-pullreq: `C` runs `gh pr checkout <n>` on the selected topic, and says so when the topic is an issue rather than a pull requestportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m Ddelete comment under cursor (forge)forge-delete-comment: `D` inside a topic's post list deletes the post under the cursor (`gh api -X DELETE .../issues/comments/<id>`), asking for a second `D` to confirm; the opening post cannot be deleted, matching forgeportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m Mcreate mark to use with topics (forge)forge-create-mark: `M` prompts for a name and adds it to the repo's known-mark list without putting it on a topicportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m bbrowse topic (open in web browser) (forge)forge-browse-topic: `b` in the forge topic list opens the selected issue/PR's URL in the system browser. Spacemacs's SPC m is the major-mode leader; in zmax the topic list is a modal component that owns its keys, so the letter lives in that mapportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m dtoggle draft pull request (forge)forge-toggle-draft: `d` flips the selected pull request between draft and ready via `gh pr ready` / `gh pr ready --undo`, refusing on issuesportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m eedit topic body (forge)forge-edit-post: `e` opens the multi-line body editor over the selected topic, pre-filled with its current bodyportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org

SPC m medit topic marks (mark is an unshared label) (forge)forge-edit-topic-marks: `m` edits the topic's marks. A mark is forge's unshared label, so zmax keeps them in .git/zmax-forge-marks.json (alongside the personal notes) and never sends them to the forge; a name typed here that is not a known mark yet is added. Server-side labels moved to `l`portedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m nedit personal note (adds to top of topic) (forge)forge-edit-topic-note: `n` edits the topic's personal note, which forge keeps locally; zmax stores it in .git/zmax-forge-notes.jsonportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m redit list of people to review an existing topic (forge)forge-edit-topic-review-requests: `r` reads comma-separated logins and runs `gh pr edit <n> --add-reviewer`, refusing on issuesportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m schange topic state (open, closed, draft, etc.) (forge)forge-edit-topic-state: `s` reads open/closed/draft/ready and runs the matching gh verb (issue|pr reopen / close, pr ready [--undo]), then re-reads the list; an unknown word is refused by nameportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m tedit topic title (forge)forge-edit-topic-title: `t` opens the title pre-filled and runs `gh issue|pr edit <n> --title` when it changesportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org
SPC m ucopy URL of topic (add to kill ring) (forge)forge-copy-url-at-point-as-kill: `u` pushes the selected topic's web URL onto the kill ringportedhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/develop/layers/+source-control/git/README.org

SPC D d rrun ediff on a directory comparing its files with their revisions if under version controlNo SPC D d r chord exists in any shipped preset (vim.rs:266-267 binds only `space D d d` and `space D d 3`); the command is reachable only by name through command_palette. Behaviour also diverges: the output is a static scratch listing, not an interactive per-file ediff session group; revision resolution is git-only (`git diff --name-only HEAD`) rather than the generic VC backend; the listing is recursive while Emacs uses one directory level; DIR resolves against the workspace root (git_exec passes `git -C <root>`); REGEXP is a Rust regex, not an Emacs regexp; empty input errors instead of defaulting to the current directory and a space-containing DIR is unparseable; untracked files are emitted despite the doc comment stating Emacs omits them; and git_exec's `Ok(stderr)`-on-empty-stdout fallback can surface a git warning line as a phantom differing file.partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org

SPC D hopen ediff documentation within EmacsSPC D h is unbound in every shipped preset (default = spacemacs::default() = vim::base() + emacs prefixes; the SPC D subtree in zmax-term/src/keymap/vim.rs:263-274 and 349-362 has no `h` entry, and spacemacs.rs binds no ediff command), so the capability is reachable only through the command palette (SPC SPC / SPC ? / A-x), never through the keybinding this spec names. The behaviour also diverges: emacs opens the Info reader on (ediff)Top with node navigation and an optional NODE argument; zmax dumps a hand-written condensation (EDIFF_MANUAL, commands.rs:15166-15195) into a scratch buffer, takes no argument, and annotates the command listing from the reverse map of the CURRENT mode only — five listed ediff commands whose docs advertise SPC D chords (m d 3, d r, m r 3, m r r, b p) are themselves unbound, so their binding column renders blank.partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org
SPC D m d 3start an ediff merge session between files with the same name in 2 directories and with a 3rd directory containing their ancestorSPC D m d 3 is bound in no shipped preset — the `space D m` prefix in keymap/vim.rs:360-362 has only `b b`, `b 3`, `f 3` children — so the command is reachable only via the palette (SPC SPC / SPC ?), and the chord string appears in the tree solely inside a doc comment (commands.rs:15761) and a registry description (commands.rs:622). No merge session is created: the command prompts once for "A B ANCESTOR [REGEXP]", then writes a read-only scratch listing splitting the A/B-common names into with-ancestor and without-ancestor buckets and instructs the user to re-run SPC D m f 3 per file, even though three_way_merge is already wired up at commands.rs:61253. Names unique to A or B are dropped instead of being reported as unmatched; MERGE-AUTOSTORE-DIR is unsupported; REGEXP is a fourth whitespace token in Rust regex syntax rather than a separate emacs-regexp prompt defaulted off…partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org
SPC D r wstart an ediff session between two regions to perform a wordwise diff (use this for small regions)Partially ported. The four-class `ediff-forward-word` tokenizer (commands.rs:14336-14373) faithfully reproduces `ediff-wordify` — verified against `emacs -Q --batch`, which prints `foo|(|bar|)|baz-qux|12|.5,|hello|!` for `foo(bar) baz-qux 12.5, hello!`, including the `12` / `.5,` split and `$var` staying one token. Two things still differ from emacs. (a) As currently built and shipped, `SPC D r w` replaces both panes with the wordified scratch text (one token per line: `foo`, `(`, `bar`, `)`, `baz`), whereas emacs shows the regions as written and overlays only the differing words; a rewrite to keep the original text and refine inside a changed row exists in the tree but does not compile (`ui/merge.rs:1658`, `String += &String`), so it is unverified and its unit tests have never run. (b) Difference *blocks* are computed line-wise by `align()`, while emacs computes them over the word stream with line structure invisible (`ediff-diff.el:566-575` resolves word indices via `ediff-goto-word` in the original buffer). Emacs reports 0 differences for `"foo bar\nbaz"` vs `"foo\nbar baz"`; a line-wise alignment of the original texts reports one. For multi-line regions the count and boundaries of difference blocks can therefore disagree with emacs even once the within-row refinement lands.partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org

Nor is the command bound at emacs's own C-x 5 C-o: that chord is absent from the C-x 5 table (spacemacs.rs:368-381), so the ONLY user path is the SPC SPC / M-x command palette. (b) Prompt/completer mismatch: ui::completers::buffer offers doc.relative_path() (zmax-term/src/ui/mod.rs:685-694) while the callback matches doc.display_name() (commands.rs:65860, document.rs:3360-3366), and display_name returns buffer_name when set. After :rename-buffer / :rename-uniquely (typed.rs:35346, :35372) the completer suggests the path but…partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org

SPC K e sstep by step edit of the last macrokmacro-step-edit-macro is ported as a real interleaved stepper, not a stub. All three previously-named gaps are closed, verified by driving target/debug/zmax over a pty in the default spacemacs preset (record `C-x (` xx `C-x )` on "abcdef", then `C-x C-k SPC`): (1) the full kmacro-step-edit-map is honoured -- y/SPC execute, d/n/DEL/C-d skip and advance, f keeps a key without executing it, !/c run the rest, C-k skips the rest but SAVES the accepted prefix (reopen shows [1/1] after y C-k), i/I/r/R/a/A all behave per kmacro.el (I and R consume exactly one key sequence; i and r loop until C-j; a executes the current key before appending; A runs the rest then appends at end), ? toggles the help block without advancing, and an unbound key re-asks at the same index rather than aborting; (2) q and C-g leave already-accepted edits applied while leaving last_kbd_macro unrewritten, matching kmacro.el:1290-1293; (3) the prompt renders as "Macro: <kept> [<pending>] <future>" on the status line with "[n/m] : Next command: <key>" and the response list in the info body. Two things still differ from emacs. TAB (act-repeat) continues on the repeated KEY rather than the dispatched command, because zmax has no command identity for a dispatched key. This is observable, not hypothetical: emacs binds both C-n and <down> to next-line, so emacs auto-acts the second; zmax executes C-n and then re-prompts at "Next command: down". It only coincides with emacs when the repeated keystroke is the identical key. Second, and outside this command's scope, macro recording keeps the terminating C-x of `C-x )`, so a two-keystroke macro steps as [1/3] with a spurious trailing <C-x>; emacs records two keys ("2*C-d" verified against emacs 30.2). Fixing act-repeat needs command identity plumbed through the compositor dispatch; fixing the trailing key belongs to kmacro_end_macro/record_macro.partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org

SPC t m stoggle system monitor (displayed in the minibuffer)Three code-verified gaps beyond "the chord is unbound". (a) Unbound chord: no `key:` token exists for SPC t m s in any preset (grep over zmax-term/src/keymap/*.rs); only the command name is reachable. (b) The reading is invisible while the user types, and the redisplay is time-gated, not idle-gated: every key event clears the status line (zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs:4664 `cx.editor.status_msg = None;`, and again at :3796 for non-key input), so after any keystroke the minibuffer is blank until the next fixed 4s tick (SYMON_REFRESH, commands.rs:14631) — and the value that reappears is up to 4s stale. symon re-displays on idle; here idleness is not consulted at all. (c) The generation guard does not cover the write it documents. The doc at commands.rs:14633-14635 claims "a quick off/on never leaves two loops writing to the minibuffer", but the liveness check reads generation only before…partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org

SPC x a ¦align region at ¦SPC x a | -> align_at_bar, bound on ASCII `|` in the spacemacs/base SPC x a subtree (keymap/vim.rs:2314); the `¦` in DOCUMENTATION.org is an org-table artifact and keybindings.el:712 binds `"xa|"`, so the ASCII-only binding and regex are correct. align_lines_repeat (commands.rs:12163) implements align-regexp's REPEAT=t: it walks column by column, pads each still-matching line's pre-delimiter chunk to max(width)+1 (SPACING 1) and emits the delimiter, so EVERY bar on a line is squared; lines that run out of matches stop contributing width and keep their tail verbatim. align_repeat_region (commands.rs:12253) applies it to the selection and, with no real region, walks outward over the contiguous delimiter-matching lines (funcs.el:1391-1401). Verified in a pty against emacs -Q --batch driving the real spacemacs/align-repeat-bar: on "a | bb | c / dddd | e | ff / xx | ccccc | d" zmax produces "a | bb | c / dddd | e | ff / xx | ccccc | d", byte-identical to the oracle, from a bare cursor and from an explicit region; a fixture with non-matching lines above and below the block confirms the outward walk stops at the same boundaries Emacs does. STILL PARTIAL for two reasons. (1) The prefix-arg `after` toggle is implemented (align_at_bar reads cx.prefix_arg(), the after branch pads to the right of the delimiter) but is UNREACHABLE: universal_argument is bound only in the emacs preset (keymap/emacs.rs:142,322) while align_at_bar is bound only in the spacemacs SPC tree, so no preset provides both. Driving C-u, C-u 4, a numeric count, and SPC u before SPC x a | all yield the no-arg output or insert a literal "|", and the oracle's after output ("a | bb | c / dddd | e | ff / xx | ccccc | d") cannot be produced. Closing this needs a prefix-argument entry point in the spacemacs preset (real spacemacs uses SPC u). (2) Under :keymap vim the SPC leader is stripped (keymap/vim.rs:2794-2810), so the binding is spacemacs-preset-only; arguably correct for a vim preset. Scope: only align_at_bar was repointed at the repeat engine. The other SPC x a * commands are generated by the same spacemacs|create-align-repeat-x macro with REPEAT=t but remain first-match-only align_region - SPC x a , was observed turning "a, bb, c" into "a , bb, c" and touching no other line. align_repeat_region is reusable for them. Caveat: the tree did not compile as delivered (unrelated concurrent breakage at commands.rs:55587, commands/typed.rs:36510, ui/merge.rs:1658), so the three new unit tests at commands.rs:46493+ have never been built or run; the above was verified from a patched clone.partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org

g pSelect pasted textPressing `g p` in zmax's shipped default preset does NOT select pasted text — it pastes. vim.rs:1118 binds normal-mode `g p` to paste_after_cursor_after (vim's gp) inside vim::base() (vim.rs:568), and spacemacs::default() (spacemacs.rs:602-641) is that same base with only C-x/C-c/C-h shift_removed and overlaid, so the vim gp binding survives untouched. grep for select_pasted_text across zmax-term/src/keymap/ returns zero hits (spacemacs.rs, vim.rs, emacs.rs, default.rs). key:normal:g p therefore resolves in the live preset but to an unrelated command; the only user route to select_pasted_text is typing its name into command_palette (bound at spacemacs.rs:391, 458, 470). Additional behavioural gaps: (1) multi-cursor — paste_impl records the marks only for the primary range (commands.rs:33754, `range_index == primary_index`) and select_pasted_text calls Selection::single (33838), so after…partialhttps://github.com/syl20bnr/spacemacs/blob/develop/doc/DOCUMENTATION.org
